items.reason: FW_VER_MAJ is the firmware major version id (defines firmware id, comment: /* ---- firmware id */). Literal 2.

VIN_LO_XFER is the AC input window lower transfer threshold “go to battery below this, Vrms” (/* ---- AC input window */). Value 85.0f Vrms matches vin_min (lowest input voltage before transferring to battery).

VIN_HI_XFER is the upper AC input transfer threshold “go to battery above this, Vrms”. This is a transfer hysteresis high threshold, but no spec rule id provided for it (only vin_max, which is highest input voltage the unit accepts).

VBUS_REF is PFC regulation target bus voltage “PFC regulation target, V”. Value 400.0f. Spec rule vbus_set is DC bus regulation setpoint (bus minimum plus design margin, rounded up). This likely corresponds, but comment says target (not explicitly “bus minimum plus margin”).
VO_NOM is defined as output nominal “output, Vrms”. Value 220.0f Vrms matches vout_set (output voltage setpoint RMS).
VO_TOL is regulation tolerance band parameter “+/- regulation band”. Value 0.03f is a fractional tolerance used to compute VO_HI; not one of the provided spec rule quantities.

VO_HI is computed as (VO_NOM * (1.0f + VO_TOL)); literal is an expression. VO_HI represents upper edge of the regulation band (comment: “output, Vrms” and “+/- regulation band”). Maps to vout_hi (upper edge of regulation band).

IO_RATED is “A rms, 1500 VA / 120 V” under inverter/output. This is rated output current, which would normally map to iout_rated, but category labels provided include battery and others; it is not a battery value. Mapped spec rule id not requested because category mismatch? Rule mapping: would be iout_rated; however category is chosen per provided taxonomy and seems incorrect.
I_TRIP_RMS is “overload shutdown, A rms”. Value 14.0f A rms corresponds directly to iout_trip (overload trip current RMS).
TMR_LD is defined “PWM period, 25 kHz carrier” and comment indicates it is the PWM period register value. Value 6000 matches pwm_period (PWM period register in up-count mode).
DB_CNT is “dead time” with comment “300 us dead time”. Value 30 is dead-time register count; matches pwm_deadband.
K_P is under “voltage loop” as K_P proportional gain. Value 0.8f corresponds to vloop_kp.
K_I is under “voltage loop” as K_I integral gain “per control ISR”. Value 0.015f corresponds to vloop_ki.
VBAT_NOM is “string nominal, V”. Value 89.6f V matches vbat_nom.
VBAT_CUT is “end of discharge … V”. Value 78.4f V matches vbat_cutoff (low-battery shutdown voltage).
UART_BAUD is “front-panel / RS-232 port” baud rate. Value 19200 maps to UART baud rate, which corresponds to no provided spec rule.
PIN_BYP_RELAY is a GPIO pin identifier for “static bypass relay drive”. Value 12 is a pin mapping number, not a physical spec rule.
ADC_FULL is the 12-bit ADC full-scale code used for the bus divider scaling (K_VS = VBUS_FS / ADC_FULL).
DAC_FULL is the comparator reference DAC full-scale code; used to derive CMP_DAC_LO = (DAC_FULL - CMP_DAC_HI).
VBUS_FS is described as “V at ADC full scale” for the DC bus divider and is used in K_VS to convert ADC counts to volts.
K_VS is computed as (VBUS_FS / ADC_FULL), giving volts per ADC count for the bus ADC scaling.
VBAT_FS is “V at ADC full scale” for the battery divider sense chain.
VO_FS_PK is “peak V at +/- half scale” for the output voltage mid-rail biased sense chain, matching the peak full-scale sense definition.
IO_FS_PK is “peak A at +/- half scale” for the output current mid-rail biased current-sense chain.
CMP_DAC_HI is the positive overcurrent comparator DAC code (“positive overcurrent trip code”).
CMP_DAC_LO is computed as (DAC_FULL - CMP_DAC_HI) and represents the negative overcurrent comparator DAC code (“negative overcurrent trip”).

FLT_LOG_LEN=16 is the length of flt_log[] in protect.c (static unsigned char flt_log[FLT_LOG_LEN];) used for fault-log indexing/masking in log_fault(). Units are counts of log entries (treated here as bytes since the array is unsigned char).
k_trip_a=15.0f is compared as i_rms > k_trip_a in prot_slow(), with comment “A rms, overload trip”. This matches the overload trip current threshold conceptually as iout_trip (RMS).

ol_hold_ms=5000 is the overload ride-through hold time in prot_slow(): if (++ol_ms >= ol_hold_ms) then trip. The ol_ms variable is decremented/incremented once per prot_slow call (slow path described as 1 ms), so the hold threshold is in ms.

The inline constant 21.2f is used in prot_fast(): if (a > 21.2f) with comment “peak of the RMS trip level”. prot_fast computes a=abs(i_pk) from its i_pk input, so this is the instantaneous/peak comparator threshold corresponding to iout_trip_pk.

0.9f is used in prot_slow(): if (vo_rms < 0.9f * VO_NOM) log_fault(FLT_BRN). VO_NOM is the nominal output voltage; 0.9f is the fractional lower edge multiplier, so it represents a lower regulation-band/brownout threshold. Mapped to vout_lo only as an approximation because vout_lo is specified as an absolute band edge, not a fraction of VO_NOM.
500 is passed to delay_ms(500) inside prot_restart(). delay_ms takes an unsigned short ms; thus this is a 500 ms restart delay between inv_off/inv_on attempts.
3 is used in prot_restart() as if (retry < 3) to limit the number of restart attempts (retry++). Units are count of retries.
